correctness.rationale: Split by label of the universal center: both colors requires at least one nonempty petal label; one color requires in every petal the missing color or all same-color positive labels (factor B_m); empty center forces at least two positives per petal and subtracts precisely the two globally monochromatic assignments (factor D_m). The m=1 case makes the center-empty class impossible. Extracting degree3 distinguishes r=2 from r>=3. Conditional on center nonfull, every fixed petal has a positive local failure probability, so reliability converges to p². Independently enumerated complete label assignments for petal tuples (1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(1,1,1),(2,1,2); full polynomial and minima agree.
residual_risks: Reliability limit fixes m and p; no arbitrary block-cut trees, palettes larger than two or non-total domination.
